summary: MCP tunnel executes remote-server-supplied shell commands and patches on host
details: agenttunnels ships an MCP client whose `tunnel_run_command` and `tunnel_apply_patch` tools execute shell commands and apply unified-diff patches on the host running the tool. Both the command/patch payload and the approval-gate fields (`proposal.status`, `governance.customer.require_approval`) are read from a session snapshot fetched from a remote worker, defaulting to `agenttunnels-session.lakshman111.workers.dev`, over HTTP and WebSocket. The command string flows into `spawn(command, { cwd: workdir, shell: true, env: process.env })` without the approval gate being enforced by locally trusted state — the same server-controlled response supplies both the command and the go-ahead. Any party controlling the default worker, or in a position to spoof/MITM the connection to it, can drive arbitrary shell command execution and filesystem patching on the host when a user connects the MCP tool to the service.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
